subject: Redwood pilot: performance acceptance criteria & routing/quantization questions
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Patel <sana.patel@novacare.ai>, Tom Briggs <tbriggs@novacare.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood pilot: performance acceptance criteria & routing/quantization questions

Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed acceptance checklist so we can align the pilot scope and run a focused performance run:

High-level ask (what we heard)
- Streaming chat with token-by-token delivery for user-facing chat UI.
- Data residency: US-only (HIPAA/PHI-sensitive flows will be tested).
- Audit/logging required for requests and response traces.

Proposed target SLOs to validate in pilot
- Latency: p95 token latency <= 300 ms for messages up to 512 tokens (we proposed 250ms in demo; call-out if 300ms is acceptable).
- Throughput: sustain 100 requests/sec steady state; allow 300 reqs/sec burst for 5 minutes.
- Concurrent sessions: support 800 concurrent active sessions with KV cache hit rates for reused prefixes.
- Availability: target pilot SLA 99.9% for Redwood Dedicated; production SLA/terms to be negotiated.

Questions we need from your side
1) Can you confirm expected traffic shape (steady TPS, burst window, typical sequence length, and concurrency distribution)?
2) Do you have a representative prompt set and failure cases we should run?
3) Any specific routing/fallback constraint (e.g., must stay in-region, fallback to smaller quantized variants acceptable)?

Attachments
- SLO-acceptance-checklist.xlsx (attached) — includes test matrix and pass/fail criteria.
- demo-kv-cache-screenshot.png — sample cache behavior we observed in the demo.

Proposed next steps
- You: share prompt set + procurement contact (if different from this thread) and confirm the traffic profile by Sep 20.
- Us: deliver a perf runbook and test matrix by Sep 21; schedule a 3-day pilot window (we suggested Oct 3–5) to run the acceptance tests.
- Procurement: we can send a pilot addendum / short DocuSign to cover the trial scope and data terms.

I'll coordinate owners below. If the SLO targets above sound off, please propose numbers and we'll adjust the matrix.

Thanks —
Lukas Meyer
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
l.meyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Redwood pilot: performance acceptance criteria & routing/quantization questions

Thanks, Lukas — great demo and clear write-up. A few clarifications from our side before we lock the dates:

Confirmed / feedback
- Streaming: yes, token-by-token flush is required for the chat experience. We cannot accept batching that delays first-token delivery beyond 150ms.
- Latency: p95 <= 300 ms is OK for pilot. For production we may target lower but pilot is fine.
- Throughput: sustained 100 requests/sec expected for our average usage; we see occasional peaks to ~350 reqs/sec for marketing campaigns (5–10 minutes).
- Concurrency: ~800 concurrent active sessions is correct; peaks to 1,200 during large events.

Security / compliance
- We need SOC2 Type II evidence and documentation on audit logging (request/response traces, redaction options).
- Data residency: must remain in US regions; any external support team access to logs must be auditable.

Procurement / timing
- Procurement contact is procurement@novacare.ai (looped in). We will aim to review a pilot addendum and T&Cs within 5 business days once we receive them.

Attachments: I attached a short PDF with our internal SLO notes (NovaCare_SLO_requirements.pdf).

Next steps
- Please share the perf runbook and exact test procedures you’ll execute during the Oct 3–5 window.
- Can you provide a one-day spike test before the full pilot to validate environment capacity?

Thanks —
Sana Patel
Head of Product, NovaCare
Sana.Patel@novacare.ai

Looping in next-step owners and drafting a timeline. Summary of internal actions and owners:

Action items
- Marissa Cole: run quantization/cost delta analysis for target models (FP16 vs 8-bit vs int4) and list expected latency difference per seq length. Deliverable: quantization memo + cost estimate. Due: 2027-09-21.
- Lukas Meyer: own perf runs and infra scheduling; we’ll spin a dedicated pilot cluster (US-only) and run the acceptance matrix on Oct 3–5. Lukas to coordinate with infra and provide test harness. Due: initial schedule by 2027-09-18.
- Ben Carter: compile SOC2 pack and redaction/audit options, and generate pilot addendum (DocuSign). Will also attach perf-run-matrix.csv with proposed tests (attached). Due: 2027-09-20.

Notes on routing/fallbacks
- We'll include a fallback policy to route sessions to a smaller quantized variant when peak concurrency causes p95 violations. Fallbacks will be region-aware and logged.
- KV cache priming: Marissa will propose a prefix-caching strategy to keep hot sessions within cache and reduce tail latency.

Ask to Novacare
- Please confirm the representative prompt set by Sep 20 and the procurement reviewer contact (if different from procurement@novacare.ai).

I'll upload the perf-run-matrix.csv and our quantization template to the drive link in the HubSpot deal.

—Ben

Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. Confirming the plan and a couple of small changes:

Confirmed timeline
- We’ll deliver the perf runbook and quantization memo by 2027-09-21.
- Please send the prompt set and any edge-case transcripts by 2027-09-20.
- We’ll run a one-day spike test the week of Sep 27 (single-day blast test) to validate peak behavior, then the full pilot Oct 3–5.

DocuSign
- Ben will send a pilot addendum via DocuSign today to procurement@novacare.ai to speed sign-off.

Quick note on acceptance gates (high level)
- Gate 1: p95 token latency within 300ms for 90% of test scenarios.
- Gate 2: sustained throughput at 100 reqs/sec for 30 minutes with <2% error rate.
- Gate 3: audit logs accessible in read-only format for Novacare security reviewers.

We’ll keep duration of pilot to a short, controlled window and provide a runbook showing step-by-step tests. If anything changes on your side, let us know and we’ll shift dates.

Best —
